assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready.

## Confirming the agent's surface (Step 2 of the assess protocol)

`muse --help` and `muse exec --help` (both re-run live on this machine, 1.2.1) expose no `--goal`/`--autonomous`/`--continue-until` flag anywhere — the same shape as claudecode's `/goal`, which also has no top-level CLI flag. `muse exec` is explicitly single-shot: 'Run one prompt non-interactively (headless)' — it accepts one prompt, runs it, and exits; there is no flag that makes it iterate on its own. So the loop, if it exists, has to live inside the interactive REPL as a slash command, exactly the pattern the SKILL warns `--help`-only scans miss.

A `strings` scan of the installed native binary (`muse-bin-1.2.1-R2847.1`, resolved via the launcher's `active_binary()`) settles it decisively:

- Slash-command registry text: `"/goal" ... "Start or manage continuous work toward a goal"` and a second, longer help string: `"/goal pins a session objective with a progress bar" ... "long multi-step effort underway"`.
- Literal command forms found: `/goal <objective>` (create/replace), `/goal edit <objective>`, `/goal resume`. Validation strings confirm the state machine behind them: `"cannot create a new goal because this session ha[s one]"`, `"only an unfinished active goal can be paused"`, `"only a paused or blocked goal can be resumed; start a replacement with /goal <objective>"`.
- A real, durable SQLite schema backs it — table `goal_revisions` with columns `status, percent_complete, current_work, next_work, token_budget, tokens_used, llm_steps_used, last_progress_at_ms, last_progress_at_steps, last_progress_reminder_fired_at_ms, wake_if_idle`, plus `goal_control_outbox`/`goal_control_receipts` for command dispatch + idempotency, and a schema constraint `"complete must be exactly 100 percent and 100 percent must be complete"`. This is progress-tracked, multi-step, persisted continuous-work state — not a cosmetic UI toggle.
- A distinct, lighter per-turn mechanism reinforces it: `reminder.agent.goal-reminder` (muse-format-spec.md §9) is a built-in micro-agent that runs on effectively every turn once a goal is active, alongside `skill-reminder`/`verify-reminder`; it only materializes its own `<parent>/subagent/<child>/session.jsonl` when it actually produces output (a live-confirmed corpus fact — the sibling `skill-reminder` child in the same run produced NO directory because its outcome was `no_reminder`). The binary also carries an `eot_goal_reminder_wait` state name, consistent with an end-of-turn gate that evaluates the reminder before a turn is allowed to fully settle.

This is agent-side, code-level, load-bearing evidence for a real self-continuing loop: the user issues `/goal <objective>` once, and the session works toward it across multiple internal steps (`llm_steps_used` increments, `percent_complete` advances) without a fresh user prompt for every iteration, converging when `percent_complete` reaches 100.

## Daemon pillar

The scenario's acceptance criteria are purely a STATE ARC: ready→working at loop start, `working` sustained across internal iterations with no `ready` between them, then `working→ready` once the goal converges. That arc is derived entirely by the EXISTING, muse-generic parser logic already proven for every other muse cell — `run.started` → `EventType=user_message` (working), `run.terminal` → `EventType=turn_done` (ready/error) (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`). Nothing goal-specific has to be parsed for the arc itself to be observable, so `daemon_capability: full` does not depend on the daemon understanding `goal_revisions` at all.

**What is genuinely unverified (carried forward, not silently resolved):** whether each internal goal iteration is emitted as a NEW `run.started`/`run.terminal` pair (which would flicker `ready`↔`working` between iterations, exactly like claudecode's Stop-hook re-prompt and copilot's autopilot continuation) or whether the `eot_goal_reminder_wait` gate holds the SAME run open across iterations (genuinely continuous `working`, closer to the scenario's strictest reading). Static binary/doc evidence cannot settle this — both claudecode and copilot's own `2-7` cells hit the identical ambiguity and it turned out to be **debounce-timing-dependent even for the SAME agent** (copilot's own re-record: 2.4s gaps produced discrete cycles, 0.9s gaps coalesced into one continuous 64s span). Per that precedent this does not change the verdict — `daemon_capability` stays `full` either way, since the arc is derivable under both shapes — but the SPEC below is deliberately written as a sustained-duration hold rather than a fixed phase count, so it does not flake against whichever shape a given recording produces. `record` should promote this from provisional to settled and flip to `observability_correction` only if the arc turns out NOT to be derivable at all (e.g. the whole run never leaves `working` for so long the daemon's own liveness heuristics misclassify it, which would be a genuinely new failure mode, not the flicker-vs-hold question).

A narrower, confirmed gap: `command.invoked` and `goal_usage_attribution` are both `Skip=true` in `parser.go` today (confirmed by `TestParseLine_CommandInvoked_Skipped` and the goal-usage-attribution dedup comment at parser.go:110-120), so the daemon does not currently surface the goal's own structured fields (objective text, `percent_complete`, iteration count) as `SessionMetrics` — the dashboard cannot show 'goal 60% complete'. That is a caveat (a narrow, real gap against a nice-to-have observable), not a `bug`: the scenario's acceptance criteria never requires goal-progress display, only the state arc.

## Driver pillar

`replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` already implements every primitive this recipe needs: `slash` is dispatched through the identical `step_send` as plain `send` (line 667), so `/goal <objective>` types and submits exactly like any other message; `step_wait_turn` (line 400) polls `turn_count()` to the run's deadline and naturally waits across however many internal iterations fire, with no re-send required between them. No driver gap.

## Vacuous-pass check

Under what condition would this cell pass while proving nothing? If the literal `/goal <objective>` text sent by the driver were for some reason not recognized as the slash command (an unconfirmed trust/permission gate silently degrading it to a plain chat message), the model could still produce a plausible ready→working→ready arc from ordinary conversation — passing every state-arc phase without the goal machinery ever firing. Because `command.invoked` is `Skip=true` in `events.jsonl` today, this can only be caught by cross-checking the RAW transcript (`session.jsonl`) for a `command.invoked` record naming `/goal ...`, not by a machine-checked spec phase. Named as a caveat and a `record`-time verification step below, not asserted in `expected.jsonl`'s phases (which stay state-arc-only per this scenario's own acceptance criteria).
caveats: UNVERIFIED, carried forward: whether the goal loop's internal continuation lands as a new run.started/run.terminal pair (discrete ready/working flicker per iteration) or holds the same run open (continuous working) cannot be settled from static evidence; both shapes keep daemon_capability=full since the arc is derivable either way, and the spec is written as a duration hold rather than a fixed phase count so it does not depend on which shape a given recording produces. record should promote this from provisional to settled.

The daemon does not surface the goal's own structured fields (objective, percent_complete, current_work/next_work, llm_steps_used) as SessionMetrics today -- command.invoked and goal_usage_attribution are both Skip=true in parser.go (TestParseLine_CommandInvoked_Skipped; parser.go:110-120). Narrow gap against a nice-to-have observable, not a bug against this scenario's acceptance criteria (state arc only).

Vacuous-pass condition: if the driver's literal '/goal <objective>' text is not actually recognized as the slash command, the model could still produce a passing-looking ready/working/ready arc from ordinary conversation. Mitigate by confirming a command.invoked record for '/goal ...' in the RAW transcript at record time (not events.jsonl, since that event is Skip=true) before trusting a green run.
cost_nonzero is asserted false: muse-spark-* is absent from the pricing catalog and no dollar cost is persisted anywhere in the corpus (strict JSON-key scan, per the shared assess context).

Only /goal <objective>, /goal edit <objective>, and /goal resume were confirmed as literal slash-command forms in the binary scan; no /goal clear or /goal cancel/pause form was found, so the recipe lets the goal converge to 100% naturally (the schema's own 'complete must be exactly 100 percent' constraint) rather than issuing an unconfirmed clear/cancel command.

sources.note: No --goal/--autonomous/--continue-until top-level flag; feature must be REPL-only if it exists.
Confirms muse exec is single-prompt headless with no continuation/goal flag -- the loop mechanism is exclusively an interactive-REPL slash command, not available via headless exec.

Slash-command help text 'Start or manage continuous work toward a goal' / 'pins a session objective with a progress bar ... long multi-step effort underway'; confirmed forms /goal <objective>, /goal edit <objective>, /goal resume; goal_revisions SQL schema (status, percent_complete, current_work, next_work, token_budget, tokens_used, llm_steps_used, last_progress_at_ms, last_progress_at_steps, wake_if_idle), goal_control_outbox/goal_control_receipts, constraint 'complete must be exactly 100 percent and 100 percent must be complete'.

Section 9 (lines 624-643): reminder.agent.goal-reminder micro-agent fires per-turn, materializes <parent>/subagent/<child>/session.jsonl only when it produces output (live-confirmed via the sibling skill-reminder child that produced none). Section 10: command.invoked records slash-command usage.

run.started -> user_message (working) / run.terminal -> turn_done (ready/error) is agent-generic and needs no goal-specific handling for the state arc. command.invoked (payloadTypeCommandInvoked, line 227) and goal_usage_attribution (line 277) are both Skip=true today -- confirmed narrow gap for goal-progress display, not the arc.
TestParseLine_CommandInvoked_Skipped confirms command.invoked is Skip=true -- '/goal' invocation itself is not a websocket-visible event today.
Precedent for /goal-shaped features: agent=yes/daemon=full/driver=ready at confidence 0.85, with the same ready/working flicker-per-iteration caveat this assessment carries for muse.

Documents the SAME debounce-dependent flicker-vs-hold ambiguity reproduced live on the SAME adapter across two recordings (2.4s gaps -> discrete cycles; 0.9s gaps -> one continuous 64s span) -- source for this assessment's duration-hold spec shape instead of a fixed phase count.

Lines 667-682: slash step dispatches through the same step_send as send (no special-casing needed for /goal); step_wait_turn (line 400) polls turn_count() to the run deadline, correctly waiting across repeated internal iterations with no re-send required.

Corpus already shows goal_usage_attribution events with goal_attribution:{mode:none} (field exists even unused); no dollar cost persisted anywhere; tokens ARE tracked (input_tokens nets out cache_read_tokens).

preconditions: muse CLI on PATH and authenticated (muse login or META_API_KEY)
irrlichd is recording (--attach or isolated coexist mode)

Fresh session with no prior goal -- /goal <objective> fails with 'cannot create a new goal because this session already has one' if a goal is already active, so this must be the session's first /goal call

This machine's muse permission profile classifies plain 'echo' bash calls as policy_decision:'allow:policy' (no approval flow) -- re-probe at record time; if a call instead produces a kind:'approval' record, the no-waiting invariant needs a different command or an approval-decision step first
setup: Driver generates a fresh session UUID + fresh cwd under <staging>/cwd/ (launch_repl, driver-interactive.sh)
Driver dismisses the untrusted-workspace trust prompt via --trust-workspace at launch (defect #1 fix, commit 0239a1bd) so the /goal slash command is not silently dropped by the modal

script.text: /goal You will run exactly two bash commands during this goal, one per internal iteration and in this exact order: first `echo iter1`, then `echo iter2`. Mark the goal complete once both have run.

verify: The RAW session.jsonl (not events.jsonl, since command.invoked is Skip=true) contains a command.invoked record naming '/goal ...' -- confirms the slash command actually fired rather than being treated as plain chat text (the vacuous-pass guard)
events.jsonl shows ready->working at loop start, sustained working activity across the internal iterations, and NO state_transition to waiting anywhere in the run
events.jsonl shows a final ready once the goal converges

session.jsonl additionally shows two distinct completed bash tool calls (echo iter1, echo iter2) as corroborating evidence of genuine multi-step autonomy -- not machine-checked by expected.jsonl, which stays state-arc-only per this scenario's acceptance criteria
